01

Unified Mobile Help Guide

One guide, several platforms — clear, organized support for web, iOS, and Android users, seamlessly.

Problem

Users on web, iOS, and Android faced confusion navigating help content. Maintaining separate guides per platform led to inconsistent documentation, duplicated effort, and a fragmented experience — users had to hunt for the right version, which created friction and drove up support tickets.

Solution

  • Designed a single unified guide that distinguishes platform-specific steps with tabs, icons, and conditional content blocks
  • Easy access to the right instructions for each device
  • One consistent tone and structure across all three platforms
  • Reduced duplication of effort for content teams

Key actions

Built a single-page tutorial per feature, separating platform-specific steps with tabs, accordions, and icons
Maintained one consistent voice and flow while still calling out key UI differences
Collaborated with product designers and QA to validate flow accuracy on real devices
Used visual indicators so users always knew which device's steps they were reading
Added platform-specific video tutorials and GIFs for hands-on engagement
Ensured a seamless experience with conditional content blocks for each OS
Prototype
Shipped

From prototype to production — the shipped article, with platform tabs at the top and iOS/Android sub-tabs nested within Mobile.

02

Restructuring Lightroom Web Help for Better Usability

Quick Start Guide — Lightroom on the web

Problem

  • The original article ran 8–10 scrolls long — overwhelming for anyone trying to complete a task
  • High bounce rate, since relevant information was hard to locate
  • One flat structure made the content hard to consume and even harder to maintain

Solution

  • Broke the single page into smaller, individually searchable articles
  • Organized topics under logical categories with intuitive navigation
  • Improved engagement by cutting scroll fatigue at the source

Key actions

Transformed one lengthy page into 56 well-organized, topic-specific articles
Implemented clear categorization and navigation for quick content discovery
Improved the experience through visual design and structured layout
Worked with product, engineering, design, and editorial to publish and maintain the live content

Two of the 56 focused articles, plus the categorized navigation list that replaced the original single long-form page.

View the live Lightroom web guide →
03

Restructured Legacy Article to Match App Layout

Knowledge Base Article — AEM Authoring

Problem

  • The legacy KB article was too long and not scannable
  • Its legacy status meant it couldn't simply be migrated into the new format
  • Users struggled to find information relevant to specific tabs inside the app

Solution

  • Created section blocks based directly on the app's in-app tabs
  • Ensured one-to-one visual and structural alignment between article and UI
  • Simplified navigation and improved overall usability
  • Bounce rate dropped, and the article became a top performer by views

Key actions

Reorganized a long, legacy article into modular, tab-based sections
Matched the HelpX layout to the app's in-app tabs for intuitive navigation
Resulted in high engagement and top-viewed status in the KB system
Improved information discoverability and reduced cognitive load

Side-by-side comparison: Lightroom Classic's Preferences UI tabs, mirrored one-to-one by the HelpX article structure.

04

Contextual CTA for Feature Adoption

Encouraging hands-on exploration through a deep-linked trial button.

Problem

  • Users often skipped new or advanced features from lack of awareness or context
  • Long discovery paths and unclear instructions reduced adoption of specific tools
  • Traditional CTAs didn't offer immediate, in-app interaction

Solution

  • Introduced a deep-linked button that takes users directly to the feature
  • Aligned the button with contextual learning content — how-tos and video tutorials
  • Improved discoverability and hands-on learning without extra app navigation

Key actions

Increased user interaction with editing tools across key pages
Provided a frictionless learning path for new and returning users alike
Helped users apply knowledge immediately, improving satisfaction and retention
Boosted time-on-feature metrics and reduced drop-off from tutorials

The same contextual CTA pattern reused across three different articles — always linking straight from the how-to into the live feature.

05

End-to-End Documentation for Call Center Software

User Manual — Amptel Dialer Call Center Software

Problem

New users struggled to understand and operate Amptel Dialer's advanced features — predictive dialing, CRM integration, call analytics. Existing support docs were fragmented, outdated, and lacked role-based guidance, driving heavy dependency on the support team.

Solution

Created a comprehensive user manual tailored to each user role — agents, supervisors, and admins — simplifying feature access and helping every role navigate its own key workflows with confidence.

↓40%
onboarding time for new agents
↓53%
support tickets via self-serve help
1

What the manual covers

Platform overview and role-based dashboards
Setup instructions for inbound and outbound campaigns
Tutorials for automatic call distribution, predictive dialers, and call recording
Step-by-step CRM integration and analytics reporting
Troubleshooting guide and quick-reference cheat sheets
Aligned product, support, and training teams through one unified set of content
